sections.history: Thiruvaduthurai is an old Shaiva centre on the Kaveri, counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams and praised by all three principal Tevaram saints — Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar. The stone temple carries Chola-period workmanship with inscriptions from the reign of Parantaka I and later rulers recording gifts and endowments. From the sixteenth century the site gained a second life as the headquarters of the Thiruvaduthurai Adheenam, a Shaiva mutt that became a major patron of Tamil Saiva Siddhanta scholarship, music and publishing.
sections.architecture: The temple is laid out on the classical Dravidian plan, with a gopuram, broad prakara corridors and a well-proportioned Chola sanctum housing the lingam of Masilamaniswarar. The goddess Oppilamulaiyammai has her own shrine. Chola stonework and later additions sit side by side, and the adjoining Adheenam complex gives the whole site the scale and quiet discipline of a living monastic town rather than a single shrine.
sections.legends: The name Gomukteeswarar comes from the tradition that a cow worshipped Shiva here and was granted liberation, mukti — a motif of the animal devotee that recurs across the Tevaram land. The place is also strongly associated with Tirumular, the Siddha author of the Tirumantiram, whose connection to this stretch of the Kaveri is held in deep reverence. The three Tevaram saints each sang of the lord here, weaving the temple into the great anthology of Tamil Shaiva hymnody.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the standard Shaiva festival calendar — Maha Shivaratri, the Tamil month of Margazhi, Pradosham and the annual Brahmotsavam — while the presence of the Adheenam adds observances tied to the mutt's own lineage of pontiffs. The guru-worship days and the anniversaries of past Adheenam heads bring scholars, musicians and devotees together in numbers.
sections.experience: Visiting Thiruvaduthurai is as much an encounter with a living institution as with an ancient temple. Alongside darshan at the sanctum, pilgrims sense the unbroken thread of Tamil Shaiva learning that the Adheenam has carried for centuries. The riverside setting, the Chola stone and the murmur of recitation give the place a grave, scholarly calm.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Thiruvaduthurai is near Kuthalam in Mayiladuthurai district, about 20 km from both Kumbakonam and Mayiladuthurai; those towns are the nearest rail heads, with frequent buses and taxis passing the temple and Adheenam.
